issues.description: Class 'Bitmap24' visibility mismatch: in the template header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) the class declares its constructors and the public API (Bitmap24(), Bitmap24(int,int), ~Bitmap24(), resize_buffer, save, set) under the private: section (lines 30-58). The example program (example_program/src/main.cpp) constructs a Bitmap24 instance and calls bitmap.resize_buffer(...) from outside the class (lines 36-38), which requires those constructors and methods to be public. The solution header (solution_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) declares the same constructors/methods as public. As provided, the template's private declarations will cause compilation errors for students trying to use Bitmap24 as shown in main.cpp.
issues.suggestedFix: Move the public API declarations (constructors: Bitmap24(), Bitmap24(int,int), destructor ~Bitmap24(), and methods resize_buffer, save, set) in the template header into a public: section so they are accessible to external callers (e.g., main.cpp). Keep internal data members private if encapsulation is desired (e.g., move width, height, data under private:). This will match the solution's visibility and allow the example program to compile.
